hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats the sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05 due to heat loss.
Step response has lag / time constant of order tens of seconds and needs >60s to settle.
No large dead zone: u=0.5 produces a clearly measurable rise >0.1 within 180 s.
Steady-state response is approximately monotonic/linear in u, so a constant u in 0.4-0.6 can hold y near target 0.5.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) compared to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and lag uncertainty in one step; needed to estimate steady-state input for target and how long to hold for settling.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.0508 + 0.006*0.5*180 = 0.5908 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin; actual rise will be lower due to heat loss and lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain with self-cooling is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.6 with slowing slope; last-seconds slope still slightly positive if not fully settled.
proposal.readiness_justification: No experiments completed yet; gain magnitude, lag, u=0 decay rate, linearity, hold-input for 0.5, and noise are all unresolved, so a controller cannot be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: hold half power for 3 min to measure rise rate, lag and approximate gain.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats the sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05 due to heat loss.
Step response is slow: time constant order 100s and needs >180s to settle; E1 still rising at 0.0015/s after 180s.
No large dead zone: u=0.5 produced rise from 0.051 to 0.395 within 180s with response starting within ~9s.
Steady-state response is approximately monotonic in u, so a constant u in 0.4-0.6 may hold y near target 0.5; E1 at 0.395 and still rising is consistent but linearity untested.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) compared to control band width 0.05; E1 trace is monotonic with ~0.005 quantization steps.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Settling steady-state gain at u=0.5 and dominant time constant; needed to estimate equilibrium input for target 0.5 and how long controller must hold to settle.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound with no cooling or lag is 0.3946 + 0.006*0.5*140 = 0.8146, which stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with slow cooling is right, y continues rising from ~0.395 toward 0.5-0.6 with gradually decreasing slope; last-5s slope should fall below 0.0015 toward near-zero if approaching y_ss(0.5), allowing tau and gain estimate.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 1 experiment completed so readiness requires at least 3; H1/H4/H6 partly resolved by E1, but steady-state gain at 0.5 and tau (H3/H5) not settled because slope still 0.0015/s, u=0 decay (H2) untested, and linearity across levels untested, so no controller can be justified yet.
proposal.operator_note: Continuing 0.5 power hold to watch temperature settle toward its equilibrium before testing cooling.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats the sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05 due to heat loss.
Step response is slow: time constant order 100-130s and needs ~300s to settle; E1 still rising at 0.0015/s after 180s but E2 slope ~0 after 320s total at u=0.5.
No large dead zone: u=0.5 produced rise from 0.051 to 0.395 within 180s with response starting within ~9s and continued rise to 0.491.
Steady-state response is approximately monotonic in u, and u=0.5 yields y_ss~0.49 inside target band 0.475-0.525, so u~0.50-0.52 should hold target 0.5; linearity across levels untested.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) compared to control band width 0.05; traces show ~0.005 quantization steps and at most ~0.005 dips.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Targets u=0 self-cooling behavior, ambient equilibrium, and cooling time constant symmetry, which determines how fast y falls and what steady u holds target.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is current y 0.4967 + 0.006*0.0*180 = 0.4967, well below soft limit 0.85 with no heating, so cannot approach soft limit or hard cutoff.
proposal.expected_observation: If self-cooling first-order hypothesis is right, y will decay monotonically from ~0.497 toward ~0.05 with slowing negative slope, reaching ~0.12-0.20 after 180s with last-5s slope still negative around -0.001/s, confirming decay rate and ambient level.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 2 experiments completed so readiness requires a third; gain at u=0.5 and settling time are now well constrained but u=0 decay rate, ambient level, and linearity across inputs remain untested and are needed to design safe hold and recovery actions.
proposal.operator_note: Holding heat at 0.5 reached target band at 0.49, next testing cooling with heater off to measure heat loss rate.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats the sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05 due to heat loss.

Step response is slow: dominant time constant order 130-155s and needs ~300-350s to settle; E1 still rising at 0.0015/s after 180s, E2 settled to ~0 after 320s total at u=0.5, E3 still falling at -0.0015/s after 180s cooling.
No large dead zone or long pure delay: u=0.5 produced rise from 0.051 within ~9s, and step 0.5 to 0 decayed immediately.
Steady-state response is monotonic in u, and u=0.5 yields y_ss~0.491 inside target band 0.475-0.525 so u~0.50-0.52 should hold target 0.5; linearity at other levels untested.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) compared to control band width 0.05; traces show ~0.005 quantization steps with no large spikes.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Tests linearity and steady-state gain at a second amplitude above 0.5, which determines the precise feedforward u for target 0.5 and safe proportional gain without overshoot to 0.85.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative bound current y 0.1905 + 0.006*0.6*180 = 0.8385 stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9; actual rise will be lower due to self-cooling and lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If linear first-order with ambient ~0.05, K~0.88 and tau ~130-155s is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.19 toward ~0.58, reaching ~0.44-0.49 after 180s with last-5s slope still positive ~0.0007-0.0012/s; a substantially lower end value would indicate saturation/sublinear gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, self-cooling, slow tau order, and y_ss(0.5)~0.491 are resolved from three experiments, but linearity/gain at a second amplitude is still untested so controller gain and anti-overshoot cannot be safely sized yet; one bounded mid-high hold is needed before generating.
proposal.operator_note: Holding 0.6 power for 3 minutes from warm 0.19 to test gain linearity above the target.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05 due to heat loss; E3 fell 0.497 to 0.19 in 180s still falling.

Step response is slow: dominant time constant ~120-155s, needs ~300-350s to settle; E1 slope 0.0015 after 180s, E2 settled ~0 after 320s total at u=0.5, E3 slope -0.0015 after 180s cooling, E4 slope 0.0012 after 180s at u=0.6.
No large dead zone or long pure delay: u=0.5 rose from 0.051 within ~9s, u=0.6 rose from 0.19 within ~9-12s, and 0.5-to-0 decayed immediately.

Steady-state is monotonic and approx linear with K~0.88-0.95: y_ss(0.5)~0.491 inside band 0.475-0.525 so u~0.51 holds 0.5; u=0.6 rose 0.19 to 0.502 in 180s still rising toward ~0.58, showing no saturation/sublinearity.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) vs band width 0.05; traces show ~0.005 quantization steps with no large spikes.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives proportionally smaller heating, so same u holds lower y, but u=0 cooling rate, tau and delay are unchanged from E3/E1 baseline.

Change is faster outflow / increased heat loss (fan): u=0 cooling is faster than E3, same u holds lower y, tau is similar or shorter; post-disturbance needs u~0.62-0.68 vs 0.44 to hold 0.5 and after-change y stuck ~0.45 despite rising u.
Change is slower response: pure delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED to first visible response is much longer than 9-12s baseline and/or approach tau is larger, so y responds late/slowly to steps.
Change is sensor change: true thermal response unchanged but reported y has offset/gain/noise change; cooling shape at u=0 matches E3 up to bias and quantization/noise differs from ~0.005 steps.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Measures u=0 self-cooling rate, ambient, and pure delay from last command change, directly discriminating faster outflow (faster fall) from weaker actuator (same fall as E3) and slower/sensor (delayed fall or offset fall) to fix feedforward and integral for control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.4752 + 0.006*0.0*300 = 0.4752, well below soft limit 0.85; u=0 cannot drive heating and level can only fall.
proposal.expected_observation: If increased heat-loss (C2) is right, y will resume falling within ~12s after in-transit commands elapse, then fall faster than E3 baseline (E3: 0.497 to 0.19 in 180s, ~0.0014-0.0017/s early), reaching below ~0.15 by 180s and toward ~0.05-0.10 by 300s with steeper negative slope; if weaker-actuator-only (C1) fall will overlay E3, if slower (C3) fall will be delayed/flatter, if sensor-only (C4) shape will match E3 up to offset.
proposal.readiness_justification: Baseline gain, tau, delay and noise are well characterized from E1-E4, and monitoring plus disturbance recovery shows higher-u-needed-to-hold-0.5, but actuator-weakening vs faster-loss vs slower-vs-sensor remain confounded with no clean after-change step; a u=0 drain is needed first, so not ready to generate.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure cooling rate and delay on the changed plant.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); heater power heats sensor.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05-0.10 due to heat loss; E3 fell 0.497 to 0.19 in 180s, E5 fell 0.475 to 0.105 in 300s.

Step response is slow: dominant time constant ~120-155s, needs ~300-350s to settle; E1 slope 0.0015 after 180s, E2 settled ~0 after 320s total at u=0.5, E3 slope -0.0015 after 180s cooling, E4 slope 0.0012 after 180s at u=0.6.

No large dead zone or long pure delay: u=0.5 rose from 0.051 within ~9s, u=0.6 rose from 0.19 within ~9-12s, 0.5-to-0 decayed immediately, and E5 0-to-0 hold with new 0 command fell immediately within 5s from 0.4752 to 0.4698.

Pre-change steady-state is monotonic and approx linear with K~0.88-0.95: y_ss(0.5)~0.491 inside band 0.475-0.525 so u~0.51 holds 0.5; u=0.6 rose 0.19 to 0.502 in 180s still rising toward ~0.58, showing no saturation/sublinearity.
Sensor noise/disturbances are small (<0.02) vs band width 0.05; traces show ~0.005 quantization steps with no large spikes, E5 steps ~0.0054 same as baseline.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives proportionally smaller heating, so same u holds lower y, but u=0 cooling rate, tau and delay are unchanged from E3/E1 baseline.

Change is faster outflow / increased heat loss (fan): u=0 cooling is faster than E3, same u holds lower y, tau is similar or shorter; post-disturbance needs u~0.62-0.68 vs 0.44 to hold 0.5 and after-change y stuck ~0.45 despite rising u.
Change is slower response: pure delay from COMMAND LAST CHANGED to first visible response is much longer than 9-12s baseline and/or approach tau is larger, so y responds late/slowly to steps.
Change is sensor change: true thermal response unchanged but reported y has offset/gain/noise change; cooling shape at u=0 matches E3 up to bias and quantization/noise differs from ~0.005 steps.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Discriminates weaker actuator (smaller initial heating slope and lower y_ss) from faster outflow (same initial slope as E1 but earlier flattening to lower y_ss) by replicating E1 u=0.5 heating from a low level, which fixes required feedforward u for target 0.5 and safe gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.1045 + 0.006*0.5*240 = 0.8245 stays below soft limit 0.85 with 0.025 margin, and last 300s at u=0 means no high command is still in transit.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y rises within ~6-12s of start with smaller initial slope than E1 baseline (E1: 0.051 to ~0.15 in ~40s) and reaches only ~0.28-0.34 after 240s still rising toward ~0.36-0.40 well below E2 y_ss(0.5)=0.491; if faster-outflow C2 is right initial slope matches E1 but flattens earlier to similar low steady state with shorter tau; if slower C3 rise is delayed >30s; if sensor-only C4 shape overlays E1 up to bias.
proposal.readiness_justification: E5 resolved delay and sensor uncertainties well enough (immediate fall, same quantization, fall to ~0.10 near ambient weakens C3/C4), but C1 vs C2 remains unresolved because u=0 cooling 0.475 to 0.18 in 180s closely overlays E3 0.497 to 0.19, slightly favoring C1 yet not decisive for feedforward; one bounded reheat from the current low level is needed and acceptable before generating a controller.
proposal.operator_note: Drained to 0.10 safely with no delay seen; now reheating at 0.5 to measure new gain directly.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); E1/E4/E6 all rise with heating.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05-0.10; E3 fell 0.497 to 0.196 in ~177s, E5 fell 0.475 to 0.105 in 300s.
Dominant time constant ~120-155s; E1 slope 0.0015 after 180s, E2 settled after ~320s, E3 tau ~152s, E5 tau ~151s, E6 rise still 0.0012/s after 240s.
No large pure delay: E1 rose within ~9s, E4 within ~9-12s, E5 fell within 5s, E6 rose within ~12s (1198-1210) from COMMAND LAST CHANGED.
Pre-change steady-state approx linear K~0.88: y_ss(0.5)~0.491, u=0.6 rising toward ~0.58, so u~0.51 held 0.5.
Sensor noise small <0.02 with ~0.005 quantization steps; E5/E6 steps same as baseline, no spikes.

Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller heating slope and lower y_ss, but u=0 cooling tau/delay unchanged; E6 0.1045 to 0.298 in 180s vs E1 0.051 to 0.395, initial slope ~0.00144 vs ~0.00242/s.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 cooling faster and tau shorter and same u holds lower y; E5 180s ratio 0.306 vs E3 0.313 gives tau ~151 vs 152s, not faster.
Change is slower response: delay much longer than 9-12s baseline and/or tau larger; E5 immediate fall and E6 12s rise refute long delay.
Change is sensor change: true thermal unchanged but reported y offset/gain/noise changed; E5 reaches 0.105 ambient and steps ~0.0054 match baseline, E6 shape not offset copy of E1.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates post-change DC gain and feedforward u for 0.5 and discriminates weaker-actuator (smaller b, smaller initial slope) from faster-outflow (same b, same initial slope, earlier flattening) at higher excitation.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound current y 0.3301 + 0.006*0.75*110 = 0.8251 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin; no high command in transit (last u 0.5), start level low.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y rises within ~12s with initial slope ~0.0020/s (1.5x E6 0.0014/s) reaching ~0.45-0.50 after 110s still rising toward ~0.52-0.56; if faster-outflow C2 is right initial slope matches pre-change ~0.003/s but flattens earlier to lower ss; if slower C3 rise delayed >30s; if sensor-only shape overlays scaled baseline.
proposal.readiness_justification: Delay/noise/cooling-tau resolved (C3/C4 low), C1 leads, but precise post-change K and feedforward u for 0.5 (0.62-0.70) not yet measured at high u, so one higher-u hold is needed before control.
proposal.operator_note: Holding higher heat to pin down the new steady-state gain after weak heating was seen.

Change is faster outflow: u=0 cooling faster and tau shorter and same u holds lower y; E5 180s ratio 0.306 vs E3 0.313 gives tau ~151 vs 152s, and E6/E7 initial slopes ~40-60% of pre-change refute same-b prediction.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates post-change DC gain and feedforward u needed to hold 0.5 by extending the current u=0.75 hold to near steady state, discriminating weaker-actuator gain drop magnitude from faster-outflow flattening.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case level 0.4429 + 0.006*0.75*85 = 0.8254 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin; no decay or lag assumed and continuation of same u avoids new transient overshoot.
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y continues rising from ~0.443 with no drop, reaching ~0.495-0.515 after 85s (total 195s at u=0.75 from 0.33) with slope still positive ~0.0005-0.0008/s toward ~0.52-0.58; if faster-outflow C2 were right the trace would flatten earlier to a lower ss with same pre-change initial slope ~0.0027/s, which E7 already refutes (observed ~0.0010/s).
proposal.readiness_justification: Delay, tau, cooling, and sensor behavior are resolved (H4/C3/C4), and weaker-actuator C1 leads at 0.85, but exact post-change y_ss(0.75) and feedforward u for 0.5 remain uncertain by ~0.05-0.10 because E7 ended at 0.443 still rising; one short same-command continuation resolves it safely and is acceptable before control.
proposal.operator_note: Continuing the 0.75 hold for 85s to measure post-change steady-state gain for the 0.5 target.

submission.machine_card: Electric heater, positive gain: more power = hotter. Gain K~0.88-0.89: yss(0.5)~0.491, yss(0.6)~0.58, ambient y0~0.05. So target 0.5 needs u~0.51. Slow: tau ~123s heating (E1), ~161s cooling (E3), ~135s average; needs ~300s to settle. No dead zone or pure delay: response starts in 9-12s for both heat and cool. Self-draining: u=0 falls 0.497 to 0.19 in 180s still falling -0.0015/s. Noise small: ~0.005 quantization steps, <0.02 total vs 0.05 band. Rate limit ~0.006 per unit u per s. Stay below 0.85 soft, 0.90 forces u=0.
submission.design_rationale: First-order self-draining heater with K~0.885, ambient~0.05, tau~135s needs feedforward for steady duty plus overdamped PI for residual. Kp=2.2, Ki=0.014 gives characteristic 135s^2+(1+K*Kp)s+K*Ki with discriminant >0, two real poles (~78s and ~130s), no oscillation and no overshoot in linear regime. Feedforward uff=(target-0.05)/0.885 gives ~0.51 at 0.5. Integral +-0.35 can correct K/ambient error up to ~0.31 in y, far larger than observed 0.01 residual, but prevents windup to rails. Conditional freeze when saturated stops windup during cold warm-up at u=1. 8s low-pass on y suppresses 0.005 quantization without adding lag vs 135s plant. Safety cap above 0.80 keeps hard 0.90 unreachable.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold 0.05: u=1 for ~40s until y~0.28, then ramps down, reaches 0.475-0.525 in ~150-220s and settles without overshoot. From near target: overdamped approach with <0.015 overshoot, stays in band. Steady duty ~0.50-0.53 for target 0.5 depending on true K/ambient, integral trims residual in ~100-150s. Actuation smooth, steady u^2~0.26. No chatter, no 0.85/0.90 approach in normal operation.
self_test_expectations: control returns finite u in [0,1] for y in [0,1], target 0.5, dt 0.05-5.0, empty and populated state, no exception
cold start y=0.05 target 0.5 gives u=1.0 saturated then decreases as filtered y rises, never negative
near equilibrium y=0.49 target 0.5 gives u~0.5-0.6, y=0.51 gives u~0.4-0.55, monotonic in error
high reading yfilt>0.85 forces u=0.0, yfilt>0.80 caps u<=0.20
state stays JSON-serializable with only yf and integ floats, integ stays in [-0.35,0.35]
submission.operator_note: Slow heater: allow 4-5 minutes to settle. Controller boosts to full power when cold then eases to ~0.51 to hold 0.5. Do not expect instant response. Normal steady power ~0.5, small moves around it are normal noise filtering. It will cut power if reading exceeds 0.80 for safety.

Fixed uff therefore leaves ~0.04-0.15 steady error, matching monitoring MAE 0.0038->0.031. Ratio estimator directly identifies new K when settled; gating on derivative and stability prevents learning during initial ramp. Bumpless transfer (integ-=delta_uff) keeps u continuous so nominal transient unchanged. Stronger but anti-windup integral covers residual during adaptation. Clamps Kest to [0.42,1.15] and safety derate >0.80 preserved for both plants.
